key_insight: BrainNext is a self-supervised 3D foundation model that learns transferable representations from large-scale unlabeled brain MRI and adapts well to multiple downstream tasks.
clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, this approach could improve MRI analysis tools across classification, segmentation, and brain-age estimation using one reusable pretrained model.
method: Masked autoencoder pretraining on 60,551 unlabeled brain MRI exams
Native 3D Bi-Directional xLSTM-UNet backbone for volumetric learning
Lightweight task-specific fine-tuning for downstream neuroimaging tasks
evidence_signal: On the FOMO 2025 Method Track, BrainNext placed second overall and ranked first for meningioma segmentation, suggesting strong cross-task transfer from large-scale pretraining.
watch_item: Performance was shown in a challenge setting, so broader clinical generalization and deployment across scanners, protocols, and patient populations still need careful validation.
paper_title: BrainNext: A General-Purpose Self-Supervised Foundation Model for Brain MRI Analysis
